The city of Sand Demis code compliance
division is responsible for enforcing
the city's municipal code and other city
regulations. Common property maintenance
concerns include but not limited to
overgrown vegetation, dilapidated
structures, fences, um trash cans that
are left out, um inoperable or abandoned
vehicles, unpermitted signs, work done
without permits, abandoned or unattended
property, and homeless encampments on
private property. More recently, code
compliance has actively addressed
homelessness related concerns involving
unattended or abandoned prop uh personal
property, lording or trespassing, and
encampments on private property.
Um, when it comes to unattended or
abandoned property on private property,
code compliance is the is the first
division that actually responds to these
concerns. Um, code compliance staff will
first determine whether the items are
located on private or public property
because there are different
requirements. As the applicable removal
process differed
on private property, staff contacts the
property owner or property management
company and request that the items be
removed and properly disposed of.
Property owners are now required to
provide advanced notice before removing
an attendant or abandoned property from
their premises and may take immediate
action upon receiving notification from
the city. If the property is not removed
within the time frame provided by staff,
code compliance will proceed with the
appropriate enforcement and compliance
measures such as issuing notice of
violations.
Throughout this process, code compliance
staff coordinates with responsive
responsible private property owners and
management companies, communicate
applicable removal requirements and time
frames, and take additional enforcement
action when voluntary compliance is not
achieved.
When it comes to encampments on private
property, uh, Kung Complice does serve
as a city's primary point of contact for
reports involving encampments and
coordinates the appropriate response and
cleanup efforts. When responding to
reports of encampments, code compliance
will first inspect the location to
verify whether individuals are currently
present at the encampment. This initial
assessment helps staff identify the
responsible property owner or in some
cases the responsible public agency and
determine the appropriate next steps. If
there are individuals present at these
encampments, code compliance will
contact Lacata, which is the city's
housing outreach coordinators to uh to
show up and provide services. After
services are either accepted or
declined, code compliance will proceed
with coordinating the removal of the
encampment and associated debris with
the property owner or government or
agency.

rarely identified within uh commercial
centers or other private property. A
majority of these encampments that we've
encountered are actually located on CALR

time, code compliance staff has
submitted more than 35 customer service
requests to CALR, supporting coordinated
cleanup activities that resulted in the
removal of more than 45 encampments.

address potential public health and
safety concerns, improve conditions
within free rightway and respond to
ongoing community concerns.

concerns and calls for loing and
